record.name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Dane County Housing Authority)
record.summary: Federal Section 8 rental assistance for very low income households in Dane County outside the City of Madison. Voucher holders rent privately owned housing and pay a share of the rent based on income.
record.benefit: A monthly rental subsidy paid to a private landlord; the household typically pays about 30% of its adjusted income toward rent.

steps: Check dcha.net for waitlist status -- all DCHA voucher waitlists are currently closed.

The Family Unification Program waitlist takes referrals from Dane County Human Services; VASH vouchers take referrals from the VA; a Coordinated Entry list takes referrals for people experiencing homelessness.
When a general waitlist reopens, apply online during the open period.

record._statusNote: Every DCHA voucher waitlist is 'Currently Closed' or referral-only as of the fetch.

of._sourceText: assists eligible low-income families and individuals in obtaining ... housing in the Dane County area. Our jurisdiction is all of Dane County except the City of Madison

except the City of Madison, which is covered by the CDA of the City of Madison -- note: a voucher can be used to move into Madison later (portability), so this scopes where you APPLY, not where you can live

of.note: All waitlists closed / referral-only. Even when open, admission is subject to HUD income limits (generally 50% of area median income), the DCHA screening criteria, and waitlist position. Cannot be resolved to eligible/ruled-out from interview facts.

eligibility._note: The HCV income rule (50% AMI, with 75% of admissions reserved for <=30% AMI) is NOT stated on the DCHA pages fetched -- they describe the program and list waitlist status. The rule is federal (24 CFR 982) and would have to be pulled from HUD, not DCHA.

rule._factsNote: Nothing new needed for what DCHA publishes (county, city). The federal income rule, if encoded, uses incomeAtOrBelow('dane-ami', 50) and existing facts -- but DCHA does not publish it, so a faithful record of THIS SOURCE is mostly manualReview.
unencodable: Waitlist closed -- the dominant fact. No amount of eligibility makes a closed list actionable.
The three referral-only routes (FUP via Dane County Human Services, VASH via the VA, Coordinated Entry for people experiencing homelessness).
HUD income limits and the 75%-of-admissions-below-30%-AMI targeting rule (not on the DCHA site).
The 'living, working, or attending training in Dane County' waitlist preference (from when the list was last open).

hops: dcha.net/hcv -- program description + waitlist status; dcha.net/waitlists for the detail. Neither states an income rule.
access.format: html-prose (no rule published beyond jurisdiction + waitlist status)

fetch.status: HTTP 200 for dcha.net/hcv. NOTE: an earlier attempt at 'danecountyhousingauthority.com' returned 'unreachable: fetch failed' -- that domain is not DCHA; the authority is at dcha.net (found via search).

scopeColocated.scopeLocation: The source publishes no eligibility figure at all -- no income limit, no percentage. This is a 'no rule published' source for a program that unambiguously HAS a rule (federal HCV). scopeColocated has nothing to measure. The honest schema value here is 'n/a -- no figure in the source'.

cost.notes: 3 fetch attempts (1 wrong domain, 2 good) + 1 search. Most of the time went to finding the real domain. The pages, once reached, were thin -- 5 minutes of reading.

surprises: A county housing authority's own website does not state its income eligibility rule anywhere -- it assumes you know Section 8 is 50% AMI, or that a caseworker will tell you. 'No rule published' is not only a small-nonprofit phenomenon; a government body running a federal entitlement can do it too.
